'''Ione Holt Grogan''' (March 4, 1891 – February 5, 1961) was an American academic, mathematician, and educator. She worked as a schoolteacher in North Carolina and Georgia for twenty-two years before joining the faculty at the [[University of North Carolina at Greensboro|Woman's College of the University of North Carolina]], where she was a professor of mathematics from 1935 to 1958. A dormitory, a residence college, and a scholarship at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro (previously the Woman's College), are named after her. Grogan was also the president of the Reviewers Club, the oldest literary club for women in North Carolina.

== Early life, family, and education ==
Grogan was born on March 4, 1891, in [[Reidsville, North Carolina]], to John Henry Grogan and Mary Alice Robertson.<ref name= uncg>{{Cite encyclopedia|url=https://encyclopedia.wp.uncg.edu/ione-grogan/|title=Ione Grogan|first=Sean|last=Mulligan|encyclopedia=Encyclopedia of UNCG History |date=June 20, 2017}}</ref><ref name= Anderson/> Through her mother, she was a descendant of the Robertson family, a [[First Families of Virginia|Virginian colonial family]], and was a relative of Captain [[John Ray Webster]].<ref name= Anderson>{{cite book| last = Anderson| first = Francis I.| title = Anderson & Irving of Rockingham County, N.C. Cox & Bryan of Onslow County, N.C. and Related Families| publisher = Avera Press| date = 1980| location = [[Wendell, North Carolina]]| pages = 46, 47, 266, 267}}</ref> Her mother was raised by an aunt and uncle, Margaret Hurt Robertson and Walter Scott Irving, Webster's great-grandparents, on their tobacco farm near [[Stoneville, North Carolina|Stoneville]] after the death of Grogan's grandmother, Nancy Montgomery.<ref name= Anderson/> Grogan had one brother, Frank Elmer Grogan.<ref name= Anderson/>

She received two degrees from the [[University of North Carolina at Greensboro|Woman's College of the University of North Carolina]], an English degree in 1913 and a mathematics degree in 1926.<ref name= uncg/> In 1928 she earned a master's degree in mathematics from [[Columbia University]].<ref name= uncg/>

== Career ==
From 1913 through the 1920s, prior to going to graduate school at Columbia, Grogan taught English at elementary, middle, and high schools in North Carolina and Georgia.<ref name= uncg/> She worked as a teacher for twenty-two years before joining the faculty at the Woman's College of the University of North Carolina in 1935.<ref name= grogan>{{Cite web|url=https://sites.google.com/a/uncg.edu/grogan-hall/about-grogan/history|title=History - Grogan Hall|website=sites.google.com}}</ref> She was a mathematics professor at the college and served as residence hall counsel for the Coit and Weil dormitories until 1958.<ref name= grogan/><ref name= uncg/><ref name= uncg2>{{Cite web|url=https://utlc.uncg.edu/residentialcolleges/grogan/about/|title=About Grogan &#124; University Teaching & Learning Commons}}</ref> She served as president of the college's Alumnae Association from 1945 to 1947.<ref name= grogan/>

While living in Greensboro, Grogan was an active member of the [[North Carolina Democratic Party]] and the Greensboro [[League of Women Voters]], and served as president of the Reviewers Club, the oldest literary club for women in North Carolina.<ref name= uncg/>

== Death and legacy ==
Grogan died on February 5, 1961. She was buried at Greenview Cemetery in Reidsville.

The Ione Holt Grogan Scholarship, as well as the Grogan Residence Hall and Grogan Residential College at the University of North Carolina at Greensboro, are named after her.<ref name= uncg/><ref name= uncg2/>
